subject: MSA + Order Attachment: ownership carveouts, training prohibitions, and feedback license
messages:
From: Jade Nolan <j.nolan@venturestream.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@venturestream.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redline: training / output ownership questions

Kimberly —

Thanks for sending the draft. Our legal team flagged a few material concerns in the MSA and the attached order attachment related to downstream output and model training rights:

- Section 3.2 (Output) as redlined appears to permit Redwood to "use" customer outputs for model training. We need explicit carveouts: VentureStream must retain ownership of outputs and Redwood must be prohibited from using verbatim customer outputs to train models that would be used to serve other customers.
- Section 6.4 (Feedback License) is very broad — it looks like a perpetual, worldwide license to use feedback and output to improve models without restriction. We can consider a narrow technical feedback license limited to de-identified telemetry and not to include customer content.
- Data retention and logging: we need a maximum retention period for logs and a guarantee that any retained logs used for product telemetry will be de-identified and aggregated.

I've attached a marked-up MSA and the Order Attachment with in-line comments. Happy to walk through with your counsel. We need to move quickly as the SOW kickoff is scheduled for 7/5.

Appreciate your help —
Jade Nolan
Sr. Counsel, VentureStream
legal@venturestream.com

Subject: RE: MSA redline: training / output ownership questions

Jade / Kimberly / team —

Thanks for the flagged points. I reviewed the redline and put together two tractable alternatives that should align with product constraints while addressing your main concerns. High level: we can offer a narrow feedback license that allows Redwood to use de-identified, aggregated telemetry and explicit opt-in training of models only when agreed in a separate training annex. We cannot accept a blanket prohibition on using aggregate telemetry for product improvements because that would materially impact our ability to operate and improve the service.

Alternative A (Preferred by Redwood):
- Output ownership: Customer retains ownership of Customer Content and Output.
- Training/Model Use: Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated telemetry and system logs for product improvement. Redwood will not use verbatim Customer Content or Output to train foundation models used to serve other customers unless there is an explicit, written training addendum and Customer consent.
- Feedback License: Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to use feedback and telemetry solely to improve the Redwood Service; Redwood will not incorporate Customer Content/Output into market-facing pretrained models without explicit permission.
- Retention: Log retention for troubleshooting and telemetry capped at 90 days by default; extended retention requires Customer approval and documented processing obligations.

Alternative B (Customer-friendly):
- Same as A but with an explicit 30-day cap on telemetry retention and stronger audit rights (quarterly review). May trigger product exceptions; could impact onboarding timelines.

I've attached a short text snippet that contains the precise clause language for Alternative A (file: proposed_feedback_clause_snippet.txt). If VentureStream is comfortable with Alternative A, I think we can finalize the MSA quickly and proceed to DocuSign. If not, let's schedule a quick call tomorrow morning to resolve remaining points.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA redline: training / output ownership questions

Aditya —

Thanks for the thoughtful alternatives. VentureStream generally prefers Alternative B (shorter retention, stronger audit rights). A few clarifications before we lock:

- Can you make the retention period 60 days (compromise)? 90 days is longer than our policy allows for customer content logs.
- We need explicit language that prohibits Redwood from deriving or claiming IP in outputs — i.e., any derivative work of the output remains Customer IP.
- For the feedback license, please include a carveout that prohibits using customer outputs or feedback containing PII to train models for other customers and requires written consent for any exception.

If you can send an updated redline with those specific edits, VentureStream is prepared to proceed to signature. We can also confirm the kickoff date if the legal path is clear.

Jade

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jade Nolan <j.nolan@venturestream.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: proposed compromise language and next steps

Jade / Samir —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the constructive compromise. Per our internal discussion, Redwood is willing to accept a 60-day default retention period (instead of 90), provided we include a limited exception path for operational needs that requires documented approval by VentureStream and an audit trail. We will also add explicit language:

- Output & derivatives: Customer retains ownership of Output; Redwood will not assert ownership over any derivative works of the Output, and any use that would incorporate Output into models used by others requires Customer's prior written consent.
- Feedback & PII: Redwood will not use feedback or Output that contains PII to train models for external customers. Any use of de-identified, aggregated telemetry for product improvement will be described in the privacy addendum.

Action items:
- Aditya to push final redline (.docx) today for VentureStream review (I asked him to reflect the 60-day retention and the explicit derivative language).
- Kimberly to circulate a short mutual action plan and send DocuSign link once VentureStream confirms the final redline.
- Laura to flag onboarding checklist items impacted by the retention exception and confirm kickoff readiness by 6/28.

If that works for you, Jade, please reply with a one-line confirmation and we'll send the DocuSign packet. We can run the brief alignment call only if any language still blocks you.

Thanks —
